prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” lawyer for every truck-accident case — the right lawyer depends on the facts of your case and the lawyer’s experience with heavy-truck litigation, FMCSA/regulatory issues, insurance-company tactics, and jury trial experience. I can help you find excellent lawyers in Dallas, but first here are practical steps and what to look for so you can pick the best attorney for your situation.

What to look for in a Dallas truck‑accident attorney
- Substantial truck-specific experience: trucking cases involve special rules (hours-of-service, driver logs, maintenance records, corporate hiring/retention practices). Ask how many truck cases they’ve handled and verdicts/settlements.
- Trial experience: many big insurers won’t offer fair settlements without a lawyer who will try the case.
- Resources to investigate: ability to hire accident reconstructionists, obtain black-box data, subpoena carrier and dispatcher records.
- Track record: membership in Million Dollar Advocates, Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, or membership in state trial lawyer associations (TTLA) is a plus.
- Clear fee and communication practices: contingency fee agreement, who pays costs up front, how they update you.
- Good local reputation and client reviews.

Where to find and vet lawyers
- State Bar of Texas lawyer referral service and directory.
- Super Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell peer reviews, Best Lawyers, and Million Dollar Advocates.
- Local bar associations and the Texas Trial Lawyers Association (TTLA).
- Google and Yelp reviews — read several recent reviews.

Key questions to ask when you call/meet
- How many truck accident cases have you handled? How many in Dallas County/DFW?
- Have you tried truck cases to verdict? Examples (without confidential specifics).
- Who in your office will handle the case day-to-day?
- How do you charge (contingency %, who pays costs)?
- What evidence will you seek (black box, driver logs, maintenance records, carrier’s safety rating)?
- What is a realistic timeline and likely range of recovery, given my injuries?
- Can you provide references from recent clients?

What documents to bring when you meet a lawyer
- Police crash report
- Photos/videos from the scene
- Medical records and bills so far
- Insurance information (yours and the truck/carrier)
- Pay stubs if lost wages claim
- Any relevant correspondences with insurers

Timing and deadlines
- Texas statute of limitations for most personal-injury/truck-accident claims is 2 years from the date of the crash (shorter in some cases); contact a lawyer quickly so evidence is preserved.

If you want, I can
- Narrow this to a short list of Dallas firms and lawyers if you give me your ZIP or neighborhood (I can’t browse the web in real time, but I can suggest well-known national and Texas firms and how to contact them, or draft an email/phone script to reach local lawyers).
- Draft a message or checklist to send to potential attorneys.

Tell me your ZIP/neighborhood and any key facts (serious injuries? commercial truck type? claim against a government vehicle?) and I’ll help you assemble a short, practical list and a phone script to contact them.
